rawItems.title: Crews rush to 'deliberate' fire at former RAF base in Hunts village
rawItems.content: Firefighters rushed to a "deliberate" fire at a derelict former RAF base in a Huntingdonshire village. Crews were called to the former RAF Upwood site on Ramsey Road near Bury on Saturday, November 21, at 3.31pm. The base opened in 1917 after a nearby farm was requisitioned for use as an emergency landing ground. Standing mostly derelict since 1994, the site has been the target of fly tipping and arson attacks for a number of years. However, there have been plans to redevelop areas into community facilities. Crews from Ramsey arrived to find a blaze on the ground floor of the derelict building and used a hose reel to extinguish it. They returned to the station by 4.10pm. A statement from Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service reads: "The cause of the fire is believed to be deliberate." Anyone with information should contact Cambridgeshire Police via their website, quoting incident 445 of November 21. Alternatively, call Crimestoppers on 0800 555111.

rawItems.title: New café and bistro on the cards for Huntingdonshire town
rawItems.content: A new café and bistro could be on the cards for Ramsey if plans are approved. Turquazze Restaurant Ltd has submitted a fresh premises licence application to Huntingdonshire District Council. Bloom and Brew would operate from the unit previously occupied by Konak Café and Grill, on 34 Great Whyte. According to the applicant, the bistro would serve breakfast, lunch and dinner, including British and Mediterranean cuisine. "The premises has approximately 70 customer seats. Alcohol will be served indoors only, with meals, by waiter service at tables. "No off-sales of alcohol are proposed," the plans said. "Bloom and Brew will operate as a family-friendly café and restaurant. "Alcohol will only be served with meals, by waiter service at tables, staff will be trained in responsible alcohol sales, public safety and child protection. "The premises will be properly managed and supervised." If approved, the venue would serve alcohol for consumption on the premises between the hours of 8am and 10.30pm Monday to Sunday. Members of the public can make representations concerning the application, either in writing or by email to licensing@huntingdonshire.gov.uk. To have your say on the application visit the district council's public register by no later than November 26. Have you got a story you want to share? items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Amenities Committee (This document contains the Referendum version of the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan, on which residents will vote in the Referendum to be held on 26 November 2026.): Approved £14,500 contract for drainage improvements across Spinningfield recreation ground, alongside installation of replacement inclusive swing sets in September.

items.title: Great Whyte Pedestrian Safety & Speed Limit Review
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Minutes (Change of Grant Holder Form): Council resolved to submit a formal request to Cambridgeshire County Council Highways for a 20mph speed zone and upgraded zebra crossing along Great Whyte, following resident traffic survey feedback.

items.title: Planning Committee Recommends Refusal for 25 Dwellings Off Oilmills Road
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Planning Meeting agenda 20261022): Unanimously recommended refusal for outline application 26/00142/OUT on grounds of highway safety on Oilmills Road, surface water flood risk, and overdevelopment beyond the settlement boundary.
